title: Physical and Chemical Changes
seo_title: Grade 5 Physical and Chemical Changes Worksheets: New Substances, Evidence and Tests
standard_text: Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on physical and chemical changes (NGSS 5-PS1-4): new substances, signs like gas bubbles, color and temperature changes, and fair tests of mixing substances. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: A chemical change makes a new substance; a physical change does not.
key_sub: Gas from mixing, a new color, a temperature change, light, a new solid or a new smell are evidence of a new substance.
body_html:
How to think about it

When substances change, ask: is there a new substance?

In a physical change the substance stays the same. Its shape, size or state changes, or it mixes or dissolves. Melting ice, cutting paper and dissolving sugar are physical changes.

In a chemical change the particles rearrange to make new substances with new properties. Rusting, burning, cooking an egg and mixing baking soda with vinegar are chemical changes.

Evidence of a new substanceExample
gas bubbles from mixingbaking soda + vinegar
a new colora nail rusting
a temperature changea hand warmer heating up
lighta glow stick
a new solid from two liquidsmilk + vinegar making curds
a new smellmilk going sour
Example

Is boiling water a chemical change? It makes bubbles.

The bubbles are water vapor.

Water vapor is still water, only as a gas.

Answer: No. It is a physical change (change of state).

Example

Vinegar is poured on baking soda. It fizzes and the cup feels cooler. What kind of change is it?

Fizzing from mixing: a new gas.

The temperature changed on its own.

Answer: A chemical change.

Common mistakes

  • Calling melting, freezing or boiling a chemical change. A change of state is physical.
  • Thinking every color change means a new substance. Mixing paints only blends colors.
  • Thinking dissolving destroys a substance. The salt or sugar can be recovered.
  • Thinking boiling bubbles are a new gas. They are water vapor.

faq.q: What is the difference between a physical and a chemical change?
faq.a: A physical change changes shape, size or state, or mixes substances, but no new substance forms. A chemical change makes new substances with new properties, such as rust from iron.

faq.q: What are signs of a chemical change?
faq.a: Gas bubbles when substances mix, a new color, a temperature change, light, a new solid forming from two liquids, or a new smell.

faq.q: Is dissolving sugar a chemical change?
faq.a: No. It is a physical change. The sugar is still there and can be recovered by evaporating the water.

faq.q: Is boiling water a chemical change?
faq.a: No. The bubbles are water vapor, which is still water. Boiling is a change of state.

items.q: What is a physical change?
c: a change in shape, size or state where no new substance forms
a change that makes a new substance
a change that can never be undone
a change that always gives off light
items.e: Cutting, melting, freezing and dissolving are physical changes. The substance is still the same.

items.q: Which is a chemical change?
items.e: Bread dough rising with yeast makes a new substance. The others only change shape, size or state, or mix things.

items.q: What kind of change is breaking a glass?
c: a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because no new substance forms
a chemical change, because it gives off light
items.e: Breaking a glass changes the shape, size, state or mixture, but the substances stay the same.

items.q: Which word best describes what happens to particles in a chemical change?
c: They rearrange to form new substances.
items.e: No particles disappear. They join together in new ways, which makes new substances.

items.q: Which is a physical change?
c: water vapor condensing on a mirror
items.e: Water vapor condensing on a mirror does not make a new substance. The others all make new substances.

items.q: Which change can usually be undone easily?
items.e: Many physical changes can be reversed: ice can melt again. Most chemical changes cannot be undone easily.

items.q: What kind of change is fireworks exploding?
c: a physical change, because only the shape changes
a physical change, because only the state changes
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
items.e: Fireworks exploding makes a new substance with new properties, so it is a chemical change.

items.q: Which is a physical change?
items.e: Stretching a rubber band does not make a new substance. The others all make new substances.

a physical change, because only the shape changes
items.e: A sliced apple turning brown makes a new substance with new properties, so it is a chemical change.

items.q: Which is a chemical change?

items.q: A new substance has

items.e: Rust is red-brown and crumbly, very different from shiny, strong iron. Different properties tell you it is a new substance.

items.q: Which is a chemical change?
items.e: A sliced apple turning brown makes a new substance. The others only change shape, size or state, or mix things.

a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because only the shape changes
items.e: Wood burning in a campfire makes a new substance with new properties, so it is a chemical change.

items.q: What kind of change is frying an egg?

items.q: What is a chemical change?
c: a change from solid to liquid
a change that makes one or more new substances
items.e: In a chemical change, the particles join in new ways to make new substances with new properties.

c: a fizzing antacid tablet in water

items.q: Ice melts into water. Is water a new substance?
c: No. Ice and water are the same substance in different states.
Yes, because it is a liquid now.
items.e: Changing state is a physical change. Water can freeze back into the same ice.

items.q: What kind of change is a puddle evaporating?
c: a chemical change, because it gives off light
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because no new substance forms
items.e: A puddle evaporating changes the shape, size, state or mixture, but the substances stay the same.

items.q: What kind of change is baking soda fizzing in vinegar?
c: a physical change, because only the shape changes
a physical change, because only the state changes
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
items.e: Baking soda fizzing in vinegar makes a new substance with new properties, so it is a chemical change.

items.q: Which is not a sign of a physical change?
c: a gas forming when two liquids mix
a change from liquid to gas when heated
items.e: A new gas from mixing can mean a new substance. Changing shape, size or state are physical changes.

items.q: What kind of change is melting butter in a pan?
c: a physical change, because no new substance forms
a chemical change, because it gives off light
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
items.e: Melting butter in a pan changes the shape, size, state or mixture, but the substances stay the same.

items.q: Mixing blue paint and yellow paint makes green paint. What kind of change is this?
c: a chemical change, because it gives off heat
a physical change: the two paints are mixed
a chemical change, because the color changed
items.e: The colors only blend. Not every color change means a new substance.

items.q: A chocolate bar melts in a hot car and then hardens again in the fridge. What kind of changes are these?
c: melting is chemical, hardening is physical
melting is physical, hardening is chemical
items.e: Melting and freezing are changes of state. The chocolate is still chocolate.

items.q: Which is a physical change?
items.e: Grinding pepper does not make a new substance. The others all make new substances.

items.q: What kind of change is an iron bike chain rusting?
c: a physical change, because only the state changes
a physical change, because only the shape changes
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
items.e: An iron bike chain rusting makes a new substance with new properties, so it is a chemical change.

items.q: Lemonade powder is stirred into water and the water turns yellow. Is a new substance formed?
c: No. The powder dissolves and colors the water, making a mixture.
items.e: The powder only dissolves. The color comes from the powder spreading through the water.

items.q: Sand and iron filings are mixed. Which shows the mixing was a physical change?
c: A magnet can pull the iron filings back out.
items.e: If you can separate the parts and they are unchanged, no new substance formed.

items.q: Which is a physical change?
items.e: Tearing a sheet of foil does not make a new substance. The others all make new substances.

items.q: Which is a physical change?

c: a chemical change, because a new substance forms

a physical change, because no new substance forms
items.e: Freezing juice into pops changes the shape, size, state or mixture, but the substances stay the same.

items.q: Which is a physical change to a piece of paper?
c: letting it turn yellow in the sun for years
items.e: Folding changes the shape only. It is still paper.

items.q: What kind of change is bread dough rising with yeast?
c: a physical change, because only the state changes
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because only the shape changes
items.e: Bread dough rising with yeast makes a new substance with new properties, so it is a chemical change.

items.q: Sugar dissolves in water. Why is this a physical change?
c: The sugar is still sugar; the water can evaporate to get it back.
items.e: Dissolving makes a mixture. Evaporate the water and the sugar crystals are left behind.

items.q: Salt water is heated until the water is gone and salt is left. What does this show about dissolving salt?
c: It was a physical change: the salt was still there.
items.e: The same salt comes back, so no new substance had formed.

items.q: What kind of change is milk going sour?
c: a physical change, because only the shape changes
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because only the state changes
items.e: Milk going sour makes a new substance with new properties, so it is a chemical change.

items.q: Water boils and bubbles form. Is this evidence of a new substance?
c: Yes, the bubbles are a new gas.
No. The bubbles are water vapor, the same substance as a gas.
items.e: Boiling is a change of state. The bubbles are water in its gas form.

items.q: Which is a physical change?
items.e: Dissolving sugar in tea does not make a new substance. The others all make new substances.

items.q: Which change makes a mixture, not a new substance?
items.e: Raisins and cereal can be picked apart. Each keeps its own properties.

items.q: Which observation is evidence that a new substance may have formed?
c: The mixture changes to a color that neither substance had.
items.e: Gas from mixing, a new color, a temperature change, light, a new solid or a new smell are signs of a chemical change. Shape and state changes are physical.

items.q: Iron rusts in wet air. Which property shows rust is a new substance?
c: Rust is the same color as iron.
Rust is a solid, like iron.
Rust is red-brown and crumbles instead of being shiny and strong.
items.e: Rust has different properties from iron, so it is a new substance.

items.q: Which observation is evidence that a new substance may have formed?
c: The substance breaks into smaller pieces.
Bubbles of gas form when two substances are mixed.
items.e: Gas from mixing, a new color, a temperature change, light, a new solid or a new smell are signs of a chemical change. Shape and state changes are physical.

items.q: A student mixes two clear liquids, and a yellow solid appears. What is the solid?
c: a new substance made by the mixing
items.e: A new solid that forms when two liquids mix is evidence of a chemical change.

items.q: A sparkler is lit and gives off bright light and sparks. What kind of change is this?
items.e: The metal powder in a sparkler burns and makes new substances, giving off light and heat.

items.q: A bubbling mixture is not always a chemical change. Which example only has a physical change?
items.e: Boiling water makes bubbles of water vapor. No new substance forms.

items.q: Which kitchen change makes a new substance?
c: toasting bread until it turns brown
items.e: Toasting changes the bread into new brown substances with a new smell and taste.

items.q: Which observation is evidence that a new substance may have formed?
c: The substance breaks into smaller pieces.
items.e: Gas from mixing, a new color, a temperature change, light, a new solid or a new smell are signs of a chemical change. Shape and state changes are physical.

items.q: Two clear liquids are mixed and a cloudy white solid appears. What evidence of a chemical change is there?
items.e: The observation shows a new solid, which is evidence that a new substance formed.

items.q: Which change gives off both light and heat as a new substance forms?
items.e: Burning wax makes new substances (gases and soot) and gives off light and heat. A light bulb changes no substance.

items.q: Which observation is evidence that a new substance may have formed?
items.e: Gas from mixing, a new color, a temperature change, light, a new solid or a new smell are signs of a chemical change. Shape and state changes are physical.

items.q: A banana peel turns black. What evidence of a chemical change is there?
items.e: The observation shows a new color, which is evidence that a new substance formed.

items.q: Why is cooking an egg a chemical change?
c: The runny egg turns into a solid with new properties that cannot change back.
The egg is in a pan.
items.e: Cooking changes the egg into new substances. You cannot uncook an egg.

items.q: A nail left outside turns red-brown and flaky. What evidence of a chemical change is there?
c: a new color and a new solid
items.e: The observation shows a new color and a new solid, which is evidence that a new substance formed.

items.q: Which observation is evidence that a new substance may have formed?

items.e: Gas from mixing, a new color, a temperature change, light, a new solid or a new smell are signs of a chemical change. Shape and state changes are physical.

items.q: Milk left out for days smells sour. What evidence of a chemical change is there?
items.e: The observation shows a new smell, which is evidence that a new substance formed.

items.q: A cake batter rises and turns brown in the oven. What evidence of a chemical change is there?
items.e: The observation shows gas and a new color, which is evidence that a new substance formed.

items.q: When baking soda and vinegar are mixed, bubbles form. What are the bubbles?
c: air that was already in the cup
items.e: The fizzing is a new gas, carbon dioxide, made by the chemical change.

items.q: Which observation is evidence that a new substance may have formed?

items.q: Mia drops the same size antacid tablet into cold water and hot water. Which variable is she testing?
items.e: Only the water temperature is different, so that is the variable she is testing.

items.e: Only the amount of baking soda changed, so that is the variable she tested.

items.q: Which safety rule is most important when testing mixtures in class?
c: Wear safety goggles and never taste the mixtures.
Mix as many things as possible.
items.e: Unknown mixtures can be harmful. Goggles protect your eyes, and you should never taste them.

items.q: In Mia's test, the tablet fizzes faster in hot water. What is the best conclusion?
c: The tablet is bigger in hot water.
Hot water makes a physical change.
The chemical change happens faster at a higher temperature.
items.e: Warmer particles move faster and react more quickly.

items.q: Ben puts a steel wool pad in a jar with a little water and seals it. After a week it is orange. Why does he also keep a dry steel wool pad in a sealed jar?
c: to see if water is needed for rusting
items.e: Comparing wet and dry steel wool shows whether water affects rusting.

items.q: Which question can be answered by mixing two substances and observing?
c: Does mixing vinegar and baking soda make a new substance?
items.e: You can test it in class: mix them, observe the bubbles and compare properties.

items.q: A student says that burning paper is a physical change because the ashes are still paper. Which evidence shows the student is wrong?
c: Ash, smoke and gases have different properties from paper, and they cannot turn back into paper.
items.e: Burning makes new substances. Ash cannot be made back into a sheet of paper.

items.q: Why do scientists repeat an investigation several times?
c: to check that the results are reliable
items.e: If the same results happen again and again, you can trust them more.

c: No, a new substance always forms.
Not completely; she can test more properties of the mixture.
items.e: Not every chemical change is easy to see. More tests (like testing with a magnet or heating) can give more evidence.

Put the same size ice cubes on two plates, add salt to one, and time both.

items.q: A team bakes two cakes: one with baking powder and one without. Only one rises. What does the baking powder do?

items.q: Two cups of milk are left out, one in a warm room and one in the fridge. Which will most likely smell sour first?

items.q: Kai wants to test whether yeast makes a gas when mixed with sugar water. What should he use as a control?

items.e: The control is identical except for the yeast, so any difference is caused by the yeast.
